# Tsumegos whose REVIEW MODE can walk a displayed ghost stone into a lost
# position for the side solving the problem.
#
# The first move of every problem listed here is still correct and still
# winning -- the defect is in the stored continuation. Following a ghost the
# panel offers leads down a branch (typically an unbranched single-child chain)
# in which the solver's own recorded moves degrade until the position is lost,
# and the final node reports a losing winrate/score.
#
# Ghost rule replicated from pwa/js/analysis.js requestAndDisplayAnalysis:
#   solver to play   -> findBestMoveFromChildren (max winrate, score tie-break)
#   opponent to play -> among %/-commented children whose subtree reaches a
#                       pass, the lowest winrate AND the lowest score (one or
#                       two ghosts); if none reach a pass, the first
#                       %/-commented child.
# Every ghost is a path the app offers, so all of them are searched. Positions
# a user reaches by free exploration (clicking a point that is not a ghost) are
# NOT counted.
#
# A problem is listed when some ghost-reachable terminal node reports under
# 50.0% for the solver at depth >= 10 plies. The depth floor excludes the
# shallow stub variations that every problem carries.
#
# Root cause: subtreeReachesPass() treats "this branch reaches a pass" as
# "this branch was pursued to a conclusion". The generator plays some low-visit
# branches out to a pass without the move quality to match, so reaching a pass
# is not evidence the line is sound.
#
# Measured 2026-08-08 against tsumegos/ (the corpus, byte-identical to what
# package_for_pwa ships):
#   13x13   501 of  38876   1.29%
#    9x9    623 of 118626   0.53%
#   total  1124 of 157502   0.71%
#
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   size  tsumego_id  worst_ghost_reachable_winrate  depth_of_that_node
